name: front-loading
prompt: Front-loading: how much of the text's value a reader already has after its first fifth — thesis, key result, and the reason to believe it delivered before the elaboration, so that stopping early costs little.

name: portable-payload
prompt: Portable payload: the text's contribution can be carried away as one or two sentences the reader could state a week later and use, as opposed to value that exists only in the experience of reading the whole.

name: read-now-premium
prompt: Read-now premium: how much a reader loses by reading this a month from now instead of today — decisions, windows, ongoing work, or conversations it feeds that will have moved on by then.

name: source-uniqueness
prompt: Source uniqueness: how hard it would be to get this text's payload anywhere else — first-hand data, direct experience, or a synthesis no other single text provides — as opposed to content many other texts also deliver.

name: canonicality
prompt: Canonicality: this is the text one would send someone to for its point — the best single statement of it that exists — rather than a derivative, a partial treatment, or a version that has since been superseded.

name: breadth-of-consequence
prompt: Breadth of consequence: how many kinds of reader would decide or act differently after reading it — across fields, roles, and levels of expertise — rather than a narrow few specialists.

name: reader-empowerment
prompt: Reader empowerment: the reader finishes more capable — holding a tool, a move, or a distinction they can apply — rather than merely informed, entertained, or alarmed.

name: misleading-if-trusted
prompt: Misleading if trusted: the chance that a reader who takes this text at face value ends up confidently wrong — through its framing, its omissions, or certainty it has not earned — regardless of how careful it looks.

name: compounding-value
prompt: Compounding value: reading this makes the reader's later reading more valuable — it supplies a frame, a vocabulary, or a prerequisite that other texts build on.

name: effort-to-value
prompt: Effort to value: the value delivered relative to the reading effort demanded — length, density, prerequisite load, and structure — so a short clear text with a real payload scores high and a long demanding one with the same payload scores low.

name: discourse-currency
prompt: Discourse currency: how much reading this lets the reader follow or join the conversations happening now around it — the text a community is actively responding to, rather than one nobody is discussing.

name: regret-if-missed
prompt: Regret if missed: how much a thoughtful reader in this text's intended audience would regret, a year later, never having read it.
